mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 6% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate exceeds 6% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises and payroll employment falls simultaneously, it indicates a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate leads to higher borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases beyond 2% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production suggests increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production rises but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates weak demand in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts fall below 1000 but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises and the federal funds rate increases, it signals tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS increases but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime, if payroll employment growth slows, it may signal late-cycle expansion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If payroll employment growth slows with low unemployment but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 40% of cases.
